proposal.summary: Gitpod versions prior to release-2022.11.2.16 have a Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH) vulnerability allowing attackers to make WebSocket connections to the Gitpod JSONRPC server using a victim’s credentials because the Origin header is not restricted, potentially leading to data extraction and full workspace takeover.
proposal.cwe_quote: There is a Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH) vulnerability that allows attackers to make WebSocket connections to the Gitpod JSONRPC server using a victim’s credentials, because the Origin header is not restricted.

AV.quote: attackers to make WebSocket connections to the Gitpod JSONRPC server using a victim’s credentials

C.quote: This can lead to the extraction of data from workspaces, to a full takeover of the workspace.

I.quote: This can lead to the extraction of data from workspaces, to a full takeover of the workspace.

A.quote: This can lead to the extraction of data from workspaces, to a full takeover of the workspace.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Immediately restrict and validate the Origin header on the JSONRPC WebSocket endpoint; backport the fix to all affected releases and notify users to update to release-2022.11.2.16 or later. Investigate logs for unauthorized websocket connections and potential workspace compromise.

evidence_quotes.quote: There is a Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH) vulnerability that allows attackers to make WebSocket connections to the Gitpod JSONRPC server using a victim’s credentials, because the Origin header is not restricted.
This can lead to the extraction of data from workspaces, to a full takeover of the workspace.
